Label: D to Sherpur
Description: This road leads to Sherpur, one of the smaller villages that surround Chainpur.  Residents frequently called this village constellation simply as “Chainpur” to outsiders.  Schools have just let out and sox children in private schools walk home in their uniforms while those in government schools do so in everyday wear.

Label: K to Naughara
Description: Chainpur’s roads have had to bear the burden of foot traffic, especially pedestrians laden with crops and possessions, and vehicles varying from bicycle rickshaws carrying passengers to trucks transporting heavy cargoes.  Along this road, businesses and residences tapered off into fields before entering the neighboring village of Naughara.

Label: See a college bus
Description: In the 2000s, a nearby college offered students from the village of Naughara daily transportation to its classrooms.  This provided yet another indication of the rising importance of tertiary education for a growing middle class.

Label: View an Indian roller
Description: Indian rollers flash their bright colors while in flight across north India.  Their Hindi name, Neelkanth (Blue-throated), references an instance in a Hindu narrative of cosmic creation.  As the primordial cosmic ocean churned, a poison emerged that the god Shiv swallowed in order to protect the nascent world.  Held in his throat, the poison turned it blue, and so “Neelkanth” became one of the deity’s names.

Label: K to L
Description: This gali (alley) leads to the neighborhoods of Jama Masjid and Marai.

Label: L to K
Description: A few Muslim tombs stood along the land behind the Jama Masjid and alongside the gali (alley) leading to the Chowk to Naughara road.

Label: N to M
Description: The concrete-covered brick buildings and well paved gali (alley) evidence the relative wealth in this part of Chainpur.

Label: Visit the family masjid
Description: For untold generations, the family inhabiting this muhalla (neighborhood) has used this small masjid (mosque).  The thin bricks suggest it may have been created during the era of Mughal rule.

Label: Enter the family masjid
Description: Sayyid Azad and Sayyid Karim entered the masjid’s courtyard through this gate.  In the past decade, their family had the mosque newly surfaced and whitewashed.

Label: DD to N
Description: Empty lots in the village have provided places for chickens and goats to feed as they wander from their owners’ homes, returning in the evening to regular meals.

Label: Buy cosmetics from a traveling salesman
Description: Traveling salesmen frequented neighbors to offer products such as fruits, vegetables, metal ware, and in this case cosmetics.  For women in strict purdah (seclusion) this has provided opportunities to shop without going to the public markets.

Label: N to DD
Description: This trail leaves the small neighborhood in which the Sayyid family lives and heads north into other muhallas.

Label: L to M
Description: The carefully-patterned brick pavement of this street afforded easier travel by foot, bicycle, scooter, motorcycle, or seldomly car.
